dispute_text: I cancelled this photo editing app in May through the account settings page and got a confirmation email. They have taken £14.99 again in July. I have not opened the app since. Please get my money back.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a monthly charge was taken after they cancelled and received a confirmation.

dispute_text: two coffees came out on my statement same time same amount but i only had the one flat white lol
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they were charged twice for a single coffee purchase.

dispute_text: Ordered a three-seater sofa in May, delivery was meant to be within six weeks. It is now August and nothing has turned up. I have emailed four times and phoned, and they keep saying it is 'with the courier' but can't give me a tracking number. I want my money back.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a paid sofa order was never delivered.

dispute_text: I have never played this game and do not know what these gem packs are. I don't recognise this £49.99 charge at all. My son uses the tablet sometimes but he says he didn't buy anything.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they did not make an in-game credit purchase, though a child has access to the device.
ambiguity_note: A family member (the child) may have made the purchase on a household device with a stored card, which would make it authorised household use rather than genuine third-party fraud.

dispute_text: Good afternoon. I cancelled my two-night stay on 20 June, well before the 48-hour deadline, and received a cancellation number. The hotel told me the refund would take 5-7 working days but it has now been over five weeks. Kind regards.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they cancelled a hotel booking within the free cancellation window and the refund has not arrived.

dispute_text: The festival got moved to a different weekend and I can't go now. I contacted them but no proper answer. Want my money back for both tickets.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder wants their money back after an event they bought tickets for was rescheduled.
ambiguity_note: The event was rescheduled rather than cancelled. It could be not_received (the service bought will not happen as sold) or refund_not_processed (the cardholder cancelled and expects a refund). Which one fits depends on the merchant's policy and whether a refund was promised.
label_note: Rule: received-or-used test. Event moved to a date the customer cannot attend and not attended = not_received.
claude_revision: category not_as_described -> not_received (received-or-used rule, set after smoke test); evidence revised

dispute_text: Sent a bouquet for my mum's birthday and she said it was half dead, brown roses and no lilies at all even though the website showed lilies. Very disappointing for £65.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says the delivered bouquet was wilted and missing flowers shown in the listing.

dispute_text: I cancelled my membership at the front desk on 15 July and the girl said it was all done. They still took August. Rip off.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a monthly membership fee was taken after they cancelled in person.

dispute_text: Order came with only the rice and the naan, no curries at all. Rider just left it and drove off. Restaurant wont answer phone. This is fraud basically.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says most items in a takeaway order were missing on delivery.
ambiguity_note: This was a partial delivery. The main items never arrived (not_received), but part of the order did, so it could also be treated as not_as_described (an incomplete or wrong order).

dispute_text: I hired a car from them in the middle of May and returned it full and undamaged. Now in September a charge for £212 has appeared on my card out of nowhere. The amount matches the hire cost so it looks like they only just put the payment through. My account was nearly empty this month.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a car hire payment from May was only charged in September.
label_note: Rule: a charge taken weeks or months late is processing_error (post-merge taxonomy).
claude_revision: category unclear -> processing_error (label set before authorisation_issue merge); evidence revised

dispute_text: i returned the phone case as it didnt fit my model, sent it tracked post on 21 july and they got it on the 23rd. still no refund 6 weeks later. ive got the tracking receipt
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they returned a phone case that the merchant received, but no refund has been issued.

dispute_text: There is a payment of £899.00 to an electronics website on my statement. I have never heard of this shop and I still have my card in my wallet. I did not buy a laptop. Please cancel this and send me a new card.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they did not make an £899 laptop purchase from an unknown online retailer.

dispute_text: The 'genuine leather' jacket is obviously plastic, it even smells like it. I complained and they said send it back, which I think I did, my partner posted a few parcels that week. Either way I want the £185 back.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a jacket advertised as genuine leather was synthetic and may have been returned.
ambiguity_note: It is unclear whether the jacket was actually sent back. If it was returned and no refund followed, refund_not_processed would fit better than not_as_described.

dispute_text: Booked and paid upfront for a full groom for my spaniel on Saturday 26th. Nobody came to the house, no call, no text. Tried rebooking and they ignored me. I paid for nothing.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a prepaid mobile grooming appointment never took place.

dispute_text: Website said my card was declined at checkout so I didn't get any order confirmation and gave up. Two days later £86.40 has left my account. I don't have an order number and nothing is being sent.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they were charged even though their payment showed as declined at checkout.

dispute_text: Paid for the marketing course, it was not what they promised on the sales video and also I asked to cancel within the first week. Still waiting. Very unhappy.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says an online course did not match its promotion and they asked to cancel but have not been refunded.
ambiguity_note: This could be not_as_described (the content differed from the sales video) or refund_not_processed (the cardholder cancelled in the first week and got no refund). The text supports both equally.
label_note: Received-or-used test: the course was received, so not not_received. No refund was promised, so H1 step 3: the complaint about the service itself.
claude_revision: category not_received -> not_as_described (label contradicted the received-or-used rule; found in v1 failure analysis)

dispute_text: I see two payments to this cycle shop, £64.50 on the 19th and £64.50 on the 20th. I was only in there once for a service. I do not know what the second one is.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they were charged twice for a single bike service.
ambiguity_note: This reads like a duplicate charge, but the cardholder says they don't recognise the second payment. If that payment was a separate transaction the cardholder never made, it could be raised as fraud_unauthorised.
claude_revision: category not_received -> processing_error (duplicate charge); evidence -> transaction_records, itemised_receipt

dispute_text: Hi, I sent the blender back in June within the 30 days because the lid didn't fit properly. They emailed to say they got it and the refund was approved. Two months on, nothing. Please help.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says the merchant confirmed receipt of a returned blender and approved a refund that has not arrived.

dispute_text: who is this?? £186 to a wine company, i dont even drink. somebody has used my card. have frozen it in the app
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they did not make a £186 purchase from an online wine seller.

dispute_text: I buy the phone as 'grade A like new' but it have big scratch on screen and battery is only 71 percent. Also the box say different memory, 64GB not 128GB. I write to seller but answer is not good.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a refurbished phone sold as like-new was scratched, had a weak battery and had less storage than advertised.

dispute_text: To whom it may concern, I wrote to this company on 30 May asking them to stop my weekly boxes, and they replied confirming the account had been closed. Despite this, a further £54.95 was taken on 14 June and a box I did not want was left on my doorstep. I would like this payment reversed.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a weekly meal kit charge was taken after the merchant confirmed their account was closed.

dispute_text: Found a £640 payment to a jewellery website I've never used. Only me and my husband live here and he swears he knows nothing about it, although he does use my laptop for work sometimes. I want it investigated.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they did not make a £640 jewellery purchase, though their spouse has access to their laptop.
ambiguity_note: The spouse may have made the purchase on a shared device with the saved card. That would make it household use rather than genuine third-party fraud.

dispute_text: MOVING DAY WAS 8TH AUGUST. VAN NEVER CAME. HAD TO PAY ANOTHER FIRM ON THE SPOT. £780 DEPOSIT GONE AND NOW THEY HAVE BLOCKED MY NUMBER.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a prepaid removals booking never took place.

dispute_text: Took in a wool suit for cleaning; came back shrunk; sleeves now sit above my wrists; shop says it's 'normal wear'; suit had been worn twice.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a suit came back shrunk and damaged after dry cleaning.

dispute_text: parked 2 hrs, app said £4.80 when i paid. statement says £48.00?? decimal in the wrong place surely
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they were charged £48.00 for parking that was shown as £4.80.

dispute_text: We booked a week at a cottage for August and paid in full in May. In June my mother was taken into hospital so I cancelled, and the letting agent agreed in writing to refund everything except a £150 admin fee. That was on 19 June. I have chased three times since and nothing has come through. I have kept every email if you need them.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says the merchant agreed in writing to refund a cancelled cottage booking but has not paid it.

dispute_text: They took £119.99 in July. I think it renewed even though I had already told them I was stopping, or maybe it was me accidentally buying the year plan while I was trying to cancel the monthly one, the app was really confusing. Either way I asked for it back and heard nothing.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder wants a £119.99 tutoring app payment returned but is unsure whether it was a renewal or an accidental one-off purchase.
ambiguity_note: It is impossible to tell whether this was a recurring renewal taken after cancellation (subscription_cancelled) or a one-off annual purchase the cardholder tried to undo and is waiting to have refunded (refund_not_processed).

dispute_text: Hello, this taxi journey was an airport run on 12 May. I paid by card in the car. The money only came out of my account on 17 September. Is this allowed? I had already budgeted for it back in May.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a May taxi fare was only charged to their account in September.

dispute_text: So the parcel came, yes, but inside was a pack of baby wipes and some kitchen roll, clearly someone else's order, and absolutely no orthopaedic dog bed, which is what I paid for. Customer service keep telling me 'the order shows as delivered', which is technically true I suppose.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says the parcel they received held someone else's items and the dog bed they ordered never arrived.
ambiguity_note: A parcel was delivered but held the wrong items, so this could also be treated as not_as_described (wrong item sent) rather than non-delivery.

dispute_text: I bought a 10-class pack in July and used maybe four. Then another £85 went out at the end of August. I never asked for a second pack and I'd already emailed the studio saying I was moving away.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a second class pack was charged after they told the studio they were leaving.
ambiguity_note: It is unclear whether the class pack auto-renews. If it is a one-off purchase with no recurring terms, the cardholder's request reads more like refund_not_processed than a charge taken after cancelling a recurring payment.
label_note: Rule H2: a second automatic charge for a pack or plan after the customer gave notice is a recurring charge.
claude_revision: cancellation_log -> transaction_records; return_cancellation_policy -> invoice_or_contract; category processing_error -> subscription_cancelled under rule H2 (set after v1 failure analysis, before v2 runs)

dispute_text: My purse was stolen on 9 July and I didn't notice until the 12th when I rang the bank. There's a payment for protein powder on the 11th? Definitely not me, I've never bought that stuff in my life.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a sports nutrition purchase was made with their stolen card.

dispute_text: Ordered a birthday cake for my daughter Amelia. They spelled it AMILIA in big letters, and it was a plain vanilla sponge when I'd paid extra for a three-tier chocolate one. Party ruined, frankly.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a custom cake was the wrong flavour and size and had the name misspelled.

dispute_text: There is a charge from the hair salon for £95 that I don't recognise. I had a cut and blow-dry there the same day and paid £65 at the desk, I have the receipt. What is the £95 for?
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they were charged £95 by a salon where they paid £65 for their appointment.
ambiguity_note: This could be a wrong-amount charge for the visit. But the cardholder says they don't recognise the £95, so if it is a separate second transaction it could be raised as fraud_unauthorised.

dispute_text: Group booking for 6. Cancelled 5 days ahead (policy says 72 hours). Got an email saying 'refund on its way'. It is not on its way. Six weeks.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they cancelled an escape room booking within the policy and the promised refund has not arrived.

dispute_text: Paid the photographer for my son's christening. We only got 12 photos when we were promised a 'full gallery 100+ images', and the ones we did get are blurry. He says the rest are 'coming' but it's been ages.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a photographer delivered only a few low-quality photos out of a promised full gallery.
ambiguity_note: Most of the gallery was never delivered (not_received), and what did arrive was poor quality (not_as_described). Both fit equally.

dispute_text: tried to order hayfever tablets, payment page said 'transaction failed' so i gave up and bought some in a shop instead. but £18.75 has gone from my card anyway and theres no order email
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they were charged even though the online payment showed as failed and no order was confirmed.

dispute_text: bought an LP from them end of june, tracking hasnt moved since 2 july 'item received by carrier'. seller says wait. ive waited. its september
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a record they ordered has not arrived and tracking has not updated in months.

dispute_text: The box looks right but the print is fuzzy, the cards are thin and some are misprinted, and the rulebook has spelling mistakes everywhere. I'm pretty sure this is a fake copy, not the official edition the listing says.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a board game sold as an official edition appears to be counterfeit.

dispute_text: Returned the petrol mower to the store on 2 June because it wouldn't start. Staff gave me a returns slip and said the refund would take 3 to 5 days. Nothing yet.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they returned a lawnmower in store and the promised refund has not arrived.

dispute_text: 5 x £50 gift cards bought at 3am on a site I've never heard of. I was asleep. My phone has a text code from that night that I never asked for.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they did not buy £250 of gift cards from an unfamiliar website.

dispute_text: 12 Jul: downgraded to the free plan in the app and saved a screenshot. 12 Aug: charged £7.99 anyway. 14 Aug: support chat says there's 'no record of cancellation'. I still have the screenshot.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a monthly storage plan was charged after they downgraded to the free plan.

dispute_text: Website showed £63.20 at checkout, everything was in pounds. My statement shows it was taken in US dollars plus a foreign transaction fee, which came to £66.40. Nobody said anything about dollars.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they were charged in a foreign currency when the price was shown in pounds.

dispute_text: paid the call out fee over the phone for a leak under my sink they said someone would come between 8 and 12 nobody came i rang at 1 at 3 and at 5 no answer i ended up paying someone else to fix it
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a plumber's prepaid call-out never took place.

dispute_text: The mattress started dipping in the middle after three weeks, nothing like the 'firm support' they advertise. I asked to use the 100-night trial and they said a courier would collect it and refund me. It's been in my hallway wrapped up for a month, nobody has come, and they keep saying the refund is 'in progress'.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a refund was promised under a trial period, but the mattress has not been collected and no money has been returned.
ambiguity_note: The mattress has not actually been returned. The core complaint is that it sagged and did not match the advert, so not_as_described may fit better than a refund for a completed return.

dispute_text: - I have not bought anything from this shop - £412.60 of books were sent to an address in another city - I still have my card - please stop this
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they did not place a £412.60 book order that was shipped to an unknown address.

dispute_text: My coach to Edinburgh on 2 August was cancelled the night before. They put me on a 6am one the next day, which was no use as my sister's wedding was that day, so I didn't take it. Want the £58 back.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder wants their fare back after their coach was cancelled and they refused the replacement journey.
ambiguity_note: This could be not_received (the journey booked was never provided) or refund_not_processed (the cardholder refused the alternative and effectively cancelled). Both fit equally.
label_note: Rule: received-or-used test. Booked journey cancelled, alternative not taken = not_received.
claude_revision: service_provided_proof -> replacement_offer; category not_as_described -> not_received (received-or-used rule, set after smoke test); evidence revised

dispute_text: Dear Sir or Madam, I collected my new varifocal spectacles on 21st June and have not been able to read with them since. The optician has checked them and agrees the lenses do not match the prescription I was given, yet they now wish to charge me again to remake them. I find this most upsetting.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says their new glasses were made to the wrong prescription and the merchant wants to charge for a remake.

dispute_text: Cancelled in July. They took August anyway and told me it was 'already processed' and I'd be refunded if I sent the box back unopened. Did that on the 6th and paid the postage myself. Still out of pocket.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a monthly box was charged after they cancelled, and the refund promised on its return has not arrived.
ambiguity_note: The charge was taken after cancelling, but the merchant agreed to refund it once the box was returned and the cardholder says they returned it. That makes refund_not_processed an equally strong reading.

dispute_text: Can you help? I tried to pay for a toy at the till on Saturday and the card reader said declined, so I put it back and left without it. Why has £34.99 been taken from my account then?
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they were charged for an in-store purchase that showed as declined and that they did not complete.

dispute_text: Our insurer paid the vet directly for my dog's operation and I have the settlement letter showing £412 paid to the practice on 22 July. The practice ALSO charged my card the same £412 when I collected him. The receptionist said she'd 'look into it' a month ago.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says the vet charged their card for a bill their pet insurer had already paid.

dispute_text: Paid £145 for a new screen + new battery. Got the phone back and the screen is new, yes, but the battery still dies by lunchtime and settings shows the original battery health. So they did half the job and kept all the money.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says only part of a paid phone repair was carried out.
ambiguity_note: The battery replacement appears never to have been done, which could be treated as not_received for that part of the service rather than a faulty repair.

dispute_text: I paid for a block of ten lessons. After three my instructor moved away and the school agreed to refund the seven I hadn't used, £245. That was in July. They keep saying 'end of the month'.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a driving school agreed to refund unused lessons but has not paid.

dispute_text: Great to know a 15-minute scooter ride I took back in June can just turn up on my card in late September. Took them three months to remember? Brilliant.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says an e-scooter ride from June was only charged in September.

dispute_text: Booked a magician for my twins' 6th birthday on 20 June and paid in full. 15 kids sat waiting for an hour and he never showed. Phone off. Website now down.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a prepaid children's party entertainer never turned up.

dispute_text: Bought a tent from them in June, no problem. But in August there's another £219 from the same shop. I haven't ordered anything else and I don't know what this is.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they did not make a second £219 purchase from a shop they had used before.
ambiguity_note: The amount matches the earlier undisputed order exactly, so this may be a duplicate or re-submitted charge (processing_error) rather than a purchase made by someone else.

dispute_text: The cleaners only did downstairs and left after two hours instead of four. I told them not to come back and cancelled the rest, but they've charged me the full £160 for the month.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder disputes a monthly cleaning charge after a poor visit and cancelling the remaining sessions.
ambiguity_note: This could be not_as_described (the cleaning was cut short and poor) or subscription_cancelled (a full recurring monthly charge after cancelling). Both fit equally.

dispute_text: got gel nails done sat, asked for nude and they came out kinda orange?? and 3 had lifted by sunday morning. they said come back for a fix but i just want my money back
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a gel manicure was the wrong colour and failed within a day.

dispute_text: Order W-2210: 120 wedding invitations, paid 20 May, marked 'dispatched' 3 June. They never came. The wedding was 28 June and we had to email everyone instead. The merchant just sends the same template reply.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a printed invitations order was marked dispatched but never arrived.

dispute_text: lost my card on a night out friday, didnt realise till sunday. theres several contactless payments at a pub i never went in, this one is £73.60. it was the card tapped not my phone so must be whoever found it
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says contactless payments at a pub were made by someone who found their lost card.

dispute_text: We cancelled our venue booking within the 14-day cooling-off period stated in the contract and received written confirmation that our £2,500 deposit would be returned in full. That was in May. It is now September. We have spoken to a solicitor but would prefer the bank resolve this.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a venue confirmed it would return a deposit after a cooling-off cancellation but has not paid.

dispute_text: I'm writing for my dad, who is 81. He emptied his storage unit and handed back the key on 10 August, and the manager signed a form to say the contract was ended. They have still taken £95 for September. We have a photo of the signed form.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a monthly storage fee was charged after the contract was ended in person.

dispute_text: Reason for dispute: overcharged. Ordered 2 wraps and chips, menu total £18.50, the lad keyed £28.50 into the machine and I didn't check before tapping. My receipt says £18.50.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they were charged £28.50 for a takeaway that cost £18.50.

dispute_text: This is a SCAM charge, I have never bought trainers for £310 in my life. My flatmate has borrowed my card before for the food shop but he says he'd never do this. The trainers apparently got delivered to our flat??
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they did not buy a £310 pair of trainers that were delivered to their own address.
ambiguity_note: The goods went to the cardholder's own address and a flatmate has used the card before. It may be use by someone they know rather than genuine third-party fraud.

dispute_text: Paid in full for carpets in three bedrooms, fitting date 12 June. Fitter didn't show. Rebooked for 26 June. Didn't show. Rebooked for 10 July. You can guess. My furniture has been in the garage for two months.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a fully paid carpet fitting has never been carried out.

dispute_text: We'd been looking forward to this for months, it was a 40th birthday present for my wife, but the pool was closed for 'maintenance', the hot stone massage was 20 minutes, not the 50 on the website, and the lunch was a sandwich. The manager apologised and said she'd sort out a partial refund, but nothing has arrived.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a spa day fell well short of what was advertised and a promised partial refund has not arrived.
ambiguity_note: The merchant agreed to a partial refund that has not been paid, so refund_not_processed is a competing reading.
label_note: Rule H1 (claim priority): a refund the merchant promised that has not arrived is classified first.
claude_revision: service_provided_proof -> product_listing; itemised_receipt -> replacement_offer; category not_as_described -> refund_not_processed under rule H1 (set after v1 failure analysis, before v2 runs)

dispute_text: I'm so sorry to bother you with this. I paid a £450 holding deposit for a room for September, but then got a place at a different university, so I cancelled before signing the tenancy, which their website says gets a full refund. They confirmed by email on 3 June. I still haven't received it and I really need it for my new deposit.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a holding deposit for student accommodation was confirmed as refundable but has not been returned.

dispute_text: There's a £240 payment to the piano teacher dated 1 September. I told her in July that my daughter was stopping. I can't remember whether I set up a payment that goes out every term or whether I paid for the autumn term in advance back in June, but she agreed to give back whatever was for autumn and hasn't.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder disputes a £240 payment to a piano teacher after stopping lessons and being promised money back.
ambiguity_note: It is unclear whether this was a recurring termly charge taken after cancellation (subscription_cancelled) or a one-off advance payment the teacher agreed to refund (refund_not_processed).

dispute_text: The transaction dated 10/09/2026 relates to an annual boiler service carried out on 6 May 2026. Payment was approved on the day via a card terminal, but the funds did not leave my account until four months later. I would like to understand whether this is permissible.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a boiler service paid for in May was only charged to their account in September.

dispute_text: Not mine. Never ordered perfume. My card was used online while it was in my drawer at home.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they did not make an online perfume purchase.

dispute_text: Made-to-measure blinds for 4 windows. Only 2 boxes arrived, and one of them is the wrong colour (grey, not oatmeal). The company says the order is 'complete'. So I've basically got one usable blind out of four.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says only half of a made-to-measure blinds order arrived and part of that was the wrong colour.
ambiguity_note: Two blinds never arrived (not_received), but one that did arrive was the wrong colour (not_as_described). The order is a mix of both.

dispute_text: Went in for a skin fade on Saturday before my mate's stag do, which is why I'd booked weeks in advance, asked for a number 2 on top, guy wasn't listening and was on his phone the whole time, took the top down to basically nothing and there's a step on one side, had to wear a hat all weekend and the lads still haven't let it go.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a haircut was not done as requested and was poorly finished.

dispute_text: I ordered a 3-month supply of lenses and cancelled the order within the hour because I picked the wrong prescription. Got an email saying 'cancelled, refund within 5 days'. A month later, nothing, and I've also noticed I was apparently signed up to 'auto-replenish', which I never ticked.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a cancelled contact lens order has not been refunded and they were enrolled in auto-replenish.
ambiguity_note: The order may have been set up as a recurring auto-replenish plan rather than a one-off purchase, which would make subscription_cancelled a competing category.

dispute_text: Paid for 2 games for 4 people at the desk. £42 has come out TWICE on 6 June, identical time, 19:42. We obviously only went once.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a single bowling payment was taken twice.

dispute_text: I deleted my profile AND cancelled the premium membership in June because I'm in a relationship now. They took another £29.99 on 21 July. I can't even log in to check anything because the profile is gone.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a premium membership fee was charged after they cancelled and deleted their account.

dispute_text: What did you buy? Family e-tickets. When? 14 August, for the 16th. What happened? The tickets were never emailed, and I checked spam. The gate wouldn't let us in without them, so we had to pay again on the day.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says e-tickets they paid for were never sent, so they could not use them.

dispute_text: Tried to buy a cordless drill and some timber on their website. Got an error saying 'payment could not be verified', so no order went through. My banking app now shows £214.50 to them as completed, not pending. Nothing has been dispatched.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they were charged after an online payment showed as failed and no order was placed.
claude_revision: category not_received -> processing_error (declined but charged); evidence -> transaction_records, authorisation_record

dispute_text: There are two £75 payments to the swim school this month. One is my son's term fees. The other I don't know about, and it has a slightly different name on the statement. Have I been charged twice or has someone used my card?
cardholder_claim: Cardholder disputes a second £75 payment to a swim school that they do not recognise.
ambiguity_note: The cardholder can't tell whether this is a duplicate of the term fee (processing_error) or a separate payment made by someone else (fraud_unauthorised). The different statement name supports either.

dispute_text: Took my car in for two new front tyres and tracking. They fitted tyres that are a different size to what's on the invoice and what the car needs. The steering pulls left. The garage says it's 'within tolerance'.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a garage fitted the wrong size tyres and the car now pulls to one side.

dispute_text: Booked a meeting room for a full-day workshop on 30 June. Cancelled on 16 June, two weeks' notice, and their terms say 7 days' notice gets a full refund. Their booking system shows it as 'cancelled - refund pending'. Still pending.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says a meeting room booking cancelled within policy has not been refunded.

dispute_text: Woke up to a welcome email for a travel data plan for a country I'm not going to, and £35 has been taken. I haven't been abroad this year. I didn't do this.
cardholder_claim: Cardholder says they did not buy a £35 travel data plan.
